questions.problem:
How can we best describe the following matrix? 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is a matrix for which all entries below the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, it is an upper triangular matrix.

It is not a lower triangular matrix or a diagonal matrix since there is a non-zero element above the diagonal: ${a}_{12}=1\ne 0.$

questions.problem: Which of the following is an upper triangular matrix?
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is a matrix for which all entries *below* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, it is an upper triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Correct Statements About a Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

- $B$ is upper triangular
- $B$ is lower triangular
- $B-{B}^{T}$ is upper triangular
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true, since all the entries below the main diagonal equal to zero:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- Statement II is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- Statement III is false, since the result of $B-{B}^{T}$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:

$$
B-{B}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

$$
A+{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
